name: Country
summary: A nation with its own territory, government and borders, drawn as a shape on the map.
wit: Lines on a map, but very serious lines.
trivia: There are 193 member states of the United Nations.
artBrief: Generic green country outline with a dashed border on a beige map tile; green, beige, dark grey. Blob shape, no real country.

name: Flag
summary: A piece of cloth with colours and symbols that stands for a country or group.
trivia: The study of flags is called vexillology.
artBrief: Plain red flag waving on a grey pole, no emblem; red, grey, white highlight. Generic, unlike any national flag.

name: Border
summary: The line where one country ends and another begins, sometimes marked by rivers or fences.
wit: Where the map says "you shall not pass".
trivia: Canada and the USA share the longest international border, about 8,890 km.
artBrief: Two flat map areas (green and yellow) split by a bold red dashed line; green, yellow, red.

name: Globe
summary: A spherical model of Earth showing the continents and oceans in their true shapes.
wit: A map that finally learned to spin.
trivia: The oldest surviving terrestrial globe, the Erdapfel, was made in Nuremberg around 1492.
artBrief: Classic desk globe on a brass stand, tilted; blue oceans, green land, gold stand.

name: Equator
summary: The imaginary line around the middle of Earth, equally distant from both poles.
wit: The planet's belt. Very hot belt.
trivia: The equator is about 40,075 km long.
artBrief: Blue-green globe with a bright red line across its middle, front view; blue, green, red.

name: South Pole
summary: The southernmost point on Earth, on the high ice sheet of Antarctica.
wit: Every direction from here is north.
trivia: Roald Amundsen's team first reached the South Pole on 14 December 1911.
artBrief: Striped barber-style marker pole topped by a small mirror ball on white snow; white, red, silver, pale blue sky.

name: Valley
summary: A low stretch of land between hills or mountains, often with a river along its floor.
trivia: Many Alpine valleys were carved into a U shape by ancient glaciers.
artBrief: Two green mountain slopes forming a V with a thin blue stream at the bottom; green, brown, blue.

name: Peninsula
summary: Land surrounded by water on three sides but still joined to the mainland.
wit: An island that never fully left home.
trivia: The word comes from Latin paene insula, meaning "almost an island".
artBrief: Top-down view of a green finger of land poking into blue sea from a larger landmass; green, blue, sand.

name: Fjord
summary: A long, narrow sea inlet filling a steep valley carved out by an ancient glacier.
wit: A glacier's scratch, filled with sea.
trivia: "Fjord" is one of the few English words borrowed from Norwegian.
artBrief: Deep blue water channel between two tall grey cliffs, viewed from the water; blue, grey, green tops.

name: Archipelago
summary: A group or chain of islands scattered across a stretch of sea.
trivia: The word originally named the Aegean Sea, dotted with Greek islands.
artBrief: Top-down blue sea with five small green islands in an arc; blue, green, sand-yellow edges.

name: Wall
summary: A long defensive barrier built along a frontier to keep out invaders.
trivia: Rome's Aurelian Walls, built in the 270s AD, still surround much of the city.
artBrief: Long crenellated stone wall running diagonally across a hill; grey stone, green hill, sky blue. Generic, no towers.

name: Temple
summary: A sacred building where people gather to worship, pray and celebrate holy days.
wit: A quiet house for big feelings.
trivia: Göbekli Tepe in Turkey, over 11,000 years old, is often called the oldest known temple.
artBrief: Simple generic shrine with a stepped base, columns and a peaked roof; cream, terracotta, gold accent. No specific faith symbols.

name: Palace
summary: A grand residence built for a ruler, filled with halls, gardens and ceremony.
wit: A castle that traded swords for banquets.
trivia: The word comes from Rome's Palatine Hill, where emperors built their homes.
artBrief: Wide symmetrical palace facade with a central dome and many windows; cream, gold, royal blue roof.

name: Skyscraper
summary: A very tall building with many floors, made possible by steel frames and elevators.
wit: Tower, but with an elevator pitch.
trivia: Chicago's Home Insurance Building (1885) is often called the first skyscraper.
artBrief: Single glass-and-steel tower with window grid seen from below; steel blue, grey, white glints. No spire.

name: Feast
summary: A large, festive meal shared by many people to mark a special occasion.
trivia: "Feast" comes from Latin festa, the same root as "festival".
artBrief: Long table seen at an angle with a roast, bread and fruit bowls; brown wood, golden food, red fruit.

name: Festival
summary: A day or season of celebration with music, food, decorations and traditions.
wit: A feast that brought the bunting.
trivia: UNESCO lists many festivals worldwide as Intangible Cultural Heritage.
artBrief: Strings of triangular bunting over a confetti burst; red, yellow, blue, green on light background.

name: Costume
summary: Traditional clothing worn to show cultural identity, often on holidays and special days.
trivia: Many traditional garments are made by hand and passed down within families.
artBrief: Generic embroidered robe on a hanger with patterned trim; deep red, gold, cream. Not any specific national dress.

name: Safari
summary: An expedition to watch wild animals in their natural habitat, especially in East Africa.
wit: Sightseeing where the sights look back.
trivia: "Safari" is the Swahili word for "journey".
artBrief: Open-top jeep with binoculars in front of an acacia tree at sunset; khaki, orange, dark green.

name: Africa
summary: The second-largest continent, home to 54 countries, the Sahara and the Nile.
wit: The continent the equator cuts neatly in half.
trivia: Africa is the only continent crossed by the equator and both tropics.
artBrief: Silhouette of the African continent in warm orange on a blue circle; orange, blue, cream outline.

name: North America
summary: The continent stretching from the Arctic to Central America, including Canada, the USA and Mexico.
wit: Big lakes, big canyons, big everything.
trivia: Greenland, the world's largest island, is geographically part of North America.
artBrief: Silhouette of North America in green on a blue circle; green, blue, white outline.

name: South America
summary: The continent of the Andes and the Amazon, home to 12 sovereign countries.
wit: Half rainforest, half mountain, all spectacular.
trivia: The Andes run about 7,000 km, the longest continental mountain range.
artBrief: Silhouette of South America in deep green on a blue circle; dark green, blue, yellow outline.

name: Oceania
summary: The region of Australia, New Zealand and thousands of Pacific islands.
trivia: Oceania takes its name from the ocean, since most of its area is Pacific water.
artBrief: Australia silhouette plus scattered island dots in a blue circle; sand-orange, blue, green dots.

name: Antarctica
summary: The icy southern continent with no permanent population, set aside for science by treaty.
trivia: Antarctica's ice holds about 70% of the world's fresh water.
artBrief: White Antarctica silhouette on a dark blue circle, seen from above; white, ice blue, navy.

name: France
summary: A Western European country known for Paris, fine cuisine, wine and the Eiffel Tower.
wit: Where lunch is a two-hour event.
trivia: France is the most visited country in the world by international tourists.
artBrief: France hexagon outline in blue with a small baguette; blue, cream, red.

name: Italy
summary: A boot-shaped Mediterranean peninsula, home of ancient Rome, the Renaissance and pizza.
wit: The boot that kicked off the Renaissance.
trivia: Italy has one of the highest numbers of UNESCO World Heritage Sites of any country.
artBrief: Italy boot outline in green kicking a small ball (Sicily) in blue sea; green, blue, white.

name: Spain
summary: An Iberian country famed for flamenco, paella, fiestas and Moorish palaces.
trivia: The region of Castile takes its name from its many castles.
artBrief: Iberian Peninsula shape in warm red-orange with a tiny castle; red, yellow, blue sea.

name: Greece
summary: A Mediterranean country of islands and ancient ruins, birthplace of democracy and the Olympics.
trivia: Greece has around 6,000 islands, but only about 200 are inhabited.
artBrief: Greek mainland and island dots in white on blue sea with a broken column; white, blue, marble grey.

name: Switzerland
summary: A mountainous Alpine country known for lakes, cheese, chocolate and clocks.
trivia: Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh.
artBrief: Switzerland outline in green with small blue lakes and a snowy peak; green, blue, white.

name: Norway
summary: A Scandinavian country of dramatic fjords, northern lights and the midnight sun.
trivia: Norway has given London a Christmas tree for Trafalgar Square every year since 1947.
artBrief: Long thin Norway outline in dark green with jagged fjord coast; dark green, blue, aurora green streak.

name: Iceland
summary: A North Atlantic island nation of glaciers, volcanoes, geysers and hot springs.
wit: Fire and ice, but mostly wind.
trivia: Iceland's parliament, the Althing, founded in 930, is one of the oldest in the world.
artBrief: Iceland island outline in white-ice with a small orange volcano glow; white, ice blue, orange.

name: Netherlands
summary: A low-lying European country of canals, windmills, tulips and bicycles.
trivia: About a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level.
artBrief: Small Netherlands outline in orange with a windmill silhouette; orange, blue water, white.

name: Germany
summary: A central European country known for castles, forests, engineering and festivals.
trivia: Germany borders nine countries, more than any other EU member.
artBrief: Germany outline in dark grey with thick border line and small forest dots; grey, green, gold outline.

name: Portugal
summary: A seafaring country on Europe's Atlantic edge, famous for explorers, fado and blue tiles.
trivia: Portugal's border with Spain, fixed in 1297, is among the oldest in Europe.
artBrief: Narrow Portugal outline in green beside big blue Atlantic waves; green, blue, tile white.

name: Russia
summary: The world's largest country by area, spanning eastern Europe and northern Asia.
wit: Two continents, one very long train ride.
trivia: Russia spans 11 time zones.
artBrief: Very wide Russia outline stretched across the tile in pale green; pale green, white, light blue.

name: India
summary: A vast South Asian country of many languages, spices, festivals and ancient temples.
wit: Twenty-two scheduled languages, one big flavour.
trivia: India is the world's largest producer of spices.
artBrief: India outline in saffron with small piles of colourful spice; saffron, green, red.

name: Nepal
summary: A Himalayan country between China and India, home to Mount Everest.
wit: A country that is mostly uphill.
trivia: Eight of the world's 14 peaks over 8,000 m lie in Nepal.
artBrief: Nepal outline in crimson with white snowy peaks along its top edge; crimson, white, blue.

name: Thailand
summary: A Southeast Asian kingdom of golden temples, tropical beaches and street food.
wit: The land of smiles and spicy noodles.
trivia: Thailand is the only Southeast Asian country never colonised by a European power.
artBrief: Thailand outline (elephant-head shape) in gold with a tiny temple spire; gold, green, blue.

name: Indonesia
summary: The world's largest archipelagic country, spread across more than 17,000 islands.
trivia: Indonesia has more active volcanoes than any other country.
artBrief: Chain of green islands stretched across blue sea; green, blue, red accent.

name: South Korea
summary: An East Asian country on the southern Korean Peninsula, known for K-pop and kimchi.
trivia: The Korean alphabet, Hangul, was created in 1443 under King Sejong.
artBrief: South Korea outline in white with small blue and red dot; white, blue, red, sea teal.

name: Cambodia
summary: A Southeast Asian kingdom, heart of the ancient Khmer Empire and Angkor.
wit: Home of the world's biggest temple.
trivia: Cambodia's national flag features Angkor Wat.
artBrief: Cambodia outline in jungle green with tiny stone towers; green, stone grey, red.

name: Vietnam
summary: A long S-shaped Southeast Asian country of rice paddies, the Mekong Delta and pho.
wit: Shaped like an S, tastes like pho.
trivia: Vietnam is one of the world's largest rice exporters.
artBrief: S-shaped Vietnam outline in red with green rice-paddy stripes; red, green, gold.

name: Jordan
summary: A Middle Eastern kingdom of desert landscapes such as Wadi Rum and the rose-red city of Petra.
trivia: Jordan's red Wadi Rum desert has stood in for Mars in several films.
artBrief: Jordan outline in rose-red over sand dunes; rose red, sand, dark brown.

name: United Arab Emirates
summary: A federation of seven emirates on the Arabian Peninsula, known for desert and record-breaking skyscrapers.
trivia: The UAE is made up of seven emirates, including Abu Dhabi and Dubai.
artBrief: UAE outline in sand colour with a tiny skyline; sand, silver, green.

name: Egypt
summary: A North African country along the Nile, home of the pharaohs, pyramids and the Sphinx.
trivia: The Greek historian Herodotus called Egypt "the gift of the Nile".
artBrief: Egypt square outline in sand with a blue Nile line running north; sand, blue, green strip.

name: Kenya
summary: An East African country of savanna, safaris, wildlife and long-distance runners.
wit: Great for running and for watching who's running.
trivia: The wildebeest Great Migration crosses into Kenya's Maasai Mara each year.
artBrief: Kenya outline in savanna yellow with an acacia tree silhouette; yellow, black, green.

name: Tanzania
summary: An East African country home to Kilimanjaro, the Serengeti and Zanzibar.
wit: Has Africa's rooftop and its best islands.
trivia: Tanzania's name joins Tanganyika and Zanzibar, which united in 1964.
artBrief: Tanzania outline in green with a small snow-capped peak; green, white, blue.

name: Morocco
summary: A North African kingdom of spice markets, desert, mountains and mosaic-tiled cities.
trivia: Morocco is only about 14 km from Spain across the Strait of Gibraltar.
artBrief: Morocco outline in terracotta with a mosaic star tile pattern; terracotta, teal, gold.

name: South Africa
summary: The country at Africa's southern tip, bordered by the Atlantic and Indian oceans.
trivia: South Africa has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.
artBrief: South Africa outline in green with blue waves on both coasts; green, blue, gold.

name: Madagascar
summary: A huge island nation off Africa's east coast, home to lemurs found nowhere else.
wit: An island with its own rulebook for animals.
trivia: Madagascar is the fourth-largest island in the world.
artBrief: Madagascar island outline in green on blue sea with a lemur tail curl; green, blue, black-white stripes.

name: Ethiopia
summary: An ancient East African highland nation, often called the birthplace of coffee.
trivia: Ethiopia uses its own calendar, which has 13 months.
artBrief: Ethiopia outline in highland green with a steaming coffee cup; green, brown, gold.

name: Zimbabwe
summary: A southern African country named after the medieval stone city of Great Zimbabwe.
wit: Named after a very impressive pile of stones.
trivia: The name Zimbabwe comes from Shona words meaning "houses of stone".
artBrief: Zimbabwe outline in gold with a small curved stone wall; gold, stone grey, green.

name: Canada
summary: The world's second-largest country, famous for lakes, forests, maple syrup and hockey.
trivia: Canada has more lakes than any other country.
artBrief: Canada outline in red with many small blue lake dots; red, blue, white.

name: Mexico
summary: A North American country of ancient pyramids, mariachi, tacos and colourful festivals.
wit: Pyramids with a side of salsa.
trivia: Mexico's Great Pyramid of Cholula is the largest pyramid in the world by volume.
artBrief: Mexico outline in green with a tiny stepped pyramid; green, terracotta, red.

name: Panama
summary: A narrow Central American country linking North and South America, famous for its canal.
trivia: Panama's S shape lets you watch the sun rise over the Pacific.
artBrief: Thin S-shaped Panama strip joining two continent edges; green, blue, red.

name: Brazil
summary: South America's largest country, home to most of the Amazon, samba and football.
wit: Plays football, grows coffee, dances samba.
trivia: Brazil has been the world's largest coffee producer for over 150 years.
artBrief: Brazil outline in green with a yellow coffee bean; green, yellow, blue.

name: Peru
summary: An Andean country of Inca heritage, Machu Picchu and Lake Titicaca.
trivia: Peru is home to around 3,000 varieties of potato.
artBrief: Peru outline in red with stepped stone terraces; red, stone grey, green.

name: Chile
summary: A long, narrow Pacific country stretching from the Atacama Desert to Patagonian glaciers.
wit: The world's longest noodle of a country.
trivia: Chile is about 4,300 km long but averages only about 177 km wide.
artBrief: Very thin tall Chile strip, sand at top fading to ice white at bottom; sand, red, white.

name: Argentina
summary: A large South American country of pampas, Patagonian glaciers, tango and asado.
wit: From ice fields to barbecue fields.
trivia: Argentina's Perito Moreno Glacier is one of the few in Patagonia that is not retreating.
artBrief: Argentina outline in sky blue with icy tip and sun dot; sky blue, white, gold.

name: Ecuador
summary: A South American country on the equator, which gave it its name, and home of the Galápagos.
trivia: "Ecuador" is Spanish for "equator".
artBrief: Ecuador outline in yellow with a red equator line crossing it; yellow, red, blue.

name: Venezuela
summary: A South American country of Caribbean coast, Andes peaks and the world's highest waterfall.
trivia: Venezuela has the world's largest proven oil reserves.
artBrief: Venezuela outline in yellow with a thin white waterfall streak; yellow, blue, white.

name: Australia
summary: A country-continent of red outback deserts, coral reefs and unique wildlife.
wit: Everything is either cute or venomous.
trivia: Australia is the driest inhabited continent.
artBrief: Australia outline in red-orange outback colour with a blue coastline; red-orange, blue, ochre.

name: New Zealand
summary: A Pacific island nation of fjords, mountains, volcanoes and Māori culture.
wit: More sheep than people, more views than both.
trivia: New Zealand was the first country to give women the vote, in 1893.
artBrief: Two NZ islands in green with a snowy ridge and fjord inlet; green, white, blue.

name: Fiji
summary: A South Pacific nation of over 300 islands, coral reefs and white beaches.
trivia: Fiji has about 330 islands, around 110 of them inhabited.
artBrief: Cluster of tiny green islands with palm on turquoise sea; turquoise, green, sand.

name: Flag of Japan
summary: The Hinomaru: a red disc on a white field, symbolising the rising sun.
trivia: The Hinomaru was legally made the national flag in 1999.
artBrief: White rectangle with centred red disc; white, red, thin grey outline.

name: Flag of France
summary: The Tricolore: three vertical bands of blue, white and red.
trivia: The Tricolore dates from the French Revolution in the 1790s.
artBrief: Vertical blue-white-red tricolour, flat; blue, white, red.

name: Flag of Italy
summary: Il Tricolore: three vertical bands of green, white and red.
trivia: Italy's tricolour was inspired by the French flag of the 1790s.
artBrief: Vertical green-white-red tricolour; green, white, red. Differs from France by green band.

name: Flag of Germany
summary: Three horizontal bands of black, red and gold.
trivia: The colours trace back to the Lützow Free Corps uniforms of 1813.
artBrief: Horizontal black-red-gold bands; black, red, gold.

name: Flag of Canada
summary: A red maple leaf on a white square between two red bands.
trivia: The maple leaf flag was first raised on 15 February 1965.
artBrief: Red-white-red vertical bands with simple 11-point red maple leaf; red, white.

name: Flag of Switzerland
summary: A white cross on a red square, one of only two square national flags.
wit: A plus sign you can salute.
trivia: Only Switzerland and Vatican City have square national flags.
artBrief: Square red flag with bold white cross; red, white. Square, not rectangular.

name: Flag of United States
summary: The Stars and Stripes: 13 red and white stripes and 50 white stars on blue.
wit: Fifty stars, thirteen stripes, zero chill.
trivia: The 13 stripes stand for the original 13 colonies.
artBrief: Simplified stars and stripes: red/white stripes, blue canton with dot-stars; red, white, navy.

name: Flag of United Kingdom
summary: The Union Jack, combining the crosses of England, Scotland and Ireland.
trivia: The Union Flag combines the crosses of St George, St Andrew and St Patrick.
artBrief: Union Jack: blue field, white and red diagonal and upright crosses; navy, red, white.

name: Flag of Greece
summary: Nine blue and white stripes with a white cross in a blue canton.
trivia: Its nine stripes are said to match the syllables of "Freedom or Death" in Greek.
artBrief: Nine horizontal blue-white stripes, blue canton with white cross; blue, white.

name: Flag of Norway
summary: A blue Nordic cross outlined in white on a red field.
wit: A cross that leans to the left.
trivia: Norway's flag has been called "the mother of flags" for holding others' colours.
artBrief: Red field, white-bordered blue off-centre Nordic cross; red, white, blue.

name: Flag of Iceland
summary: A red Nordic cross outlined in white on a blue field.
wit: Norway's flag, inverted by the sea.
trivia: The colours stand for fire, ice and the sky or mountains.
artBrief: Blue field, white-bordered red Nordic cross; blue, white, red. Inverse of Norway icon.

name: Flag of Netherlands
summary: Three horizontal bands of red, white and blue.
trivia: It is one of the oldest tricolours; the red stripe was once orange.
artBrief: Horizontal red-white-blue bands; red, white, blue. Horizontal, unlike France.

name: Flag of Russia
summary: Three horizontal bands of white, blue and red.
wit: The Netherlands, upside down and re-shuffled.
trivia: Its white-blue-red tricolour dates back to the late 1600s.
artBrief: Horizontal white-blue-red bands; white, blue, red. White on top distinguishes it.

name: Flag of India
summary: The Tiranga: saffron, white and green bands with a navy wheel of 24 spokes.
trivia: The navy wheel in the centre is the Ashoka Chakra, with 24 spokes.
artBrief: Horizontal saffron-white-green bands, small navy spoked wheel at centre; saffron, white, green, navy.

name: Flag of Nepal
summary: Two stacked crimson pennants with blue borders and white sun and moon.
wit: The only flag that refuses to be a rectangle.
trivia: Nepal's is the only national flag that is not rectangular.
artBrief: Two stacked crimson triangles with blue edge, white moon top and sun below; crimson, blue, white.

name: Flag of China
summary: A red field with one large and four small yellow stars.
trivia: The flag was first raised on 1 October 1949.
artBrief: Red rectangle, big yellow star top-left with four small stars arcing; red, yellow.

name: Flag of South Korea
summary: The Taegukgi: a red and blue yin-yang circle with four black trigrams on white.
trivia: The four trigrams stand for heaven, earth, water and fire.
artBrief: White field, central red-over-blue circle, four black bar trigrams at corners; white, red, blue, black.

name: Flag of Thailand
summary: Five horizontal stripes of red, white, blue, white and red.
trivia: The Trairanga flag was adopted in 1917; its blue stripe is double width.
artBrief: Horizontal red-white-wide blue-white-red stripes; red, white, blue.

name: Flag of Indonesia
summary: Two equal horizontal bands of red over white, called Sang Saka Merah-Putih.
trivia: It is almost identical to Monaco's flag, differing only in proportions.
artBrief: Red top half, white bottom half; red, white. Wider ratio than Poland-style icons.

name: Flag of Vietnam
summary: A yellow five-pointed star on a red field.
wit: One star, one big red stage.
trivia: The five points of the star are often said to represent workers, farmers, soldiers, intellectuals and youth.
artBrief: Red rectangle with big centred yellow star; red, yellow.

name: Flag of Tanzania
summary: Green and blue triangles split by a yellow-edged black diagonal band.
trivia: It merges the flags of Tanganyika and Zanzibar from 1964.
artBrief: Diagonal black band edged yellow, green upper-left, blue lower-right; green, blue, black, yellow.

name: Flag of South Africa
summary: A sideways green Y edged in white and gold, with red, blue and black fields.
trivia: It was adopted in 1994 and has six colours.
artBrief: Horizontal Y shape in green with white and gold edges, black triangle, red top, blue bottom.

name: Flag of Morocco
summary: A green five-pointed interlaced star on a red field.
wit: Red with a green star outline.
trivia: The green star is a pentagram known as the Seal of Solomon.
artBrief: Red rectangle with green outlined pentagram; red, green.

name: Flag of Panama
summary: Four quarters of white and colour, with one blue and one red star.
trivia: Its blue and red stand for the country's two historic political parties.
artBrief: Quartered flag: white with blue star, red, blue, white with red star; white, red, blue.

name: Flag of Chile
summary: White and red bands with a blue canton holding a single white star.
wit: The lone star of the south.
trivia: Chile's flag is nicknamed La Estrella Solitaria, "the lone star".
artBrief: Upper white band, lower red band, blue square top-left with white star; white, red, blue.

name: Great Pyramid of Giza
summary: The largest of the Giza pyramids, built as a tomb for Pharaoh Khufu around 2560 BC.
trivia: It was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for about 3,800 years.
artBrief: Single huge sand-gold pyramid with smaller ones behind, desert horizon; gold, sand, blue sky.

name: Great Sphinx of Giza
summary: A colossal limestone statue with a lion's body and a human head, guarding the Giza plateau.
wit: Still waiting for the right answer.
trivia: It is about 73 m long and 20 m high.
artBrief: Side view of the reclining Sphinx with a pyramid tip behind; sand, ochre, blue sky.

name: Suez Canal
summary: An Egyptian canal linking the Mediterranean and Red seas, opened in 1869.
trivia: It lets ships avoid the long voyage around Africa.
artBrief: Straight blue canal through sand with a container ship; sand, blue, red ship.

name: Eiffel Tower
summary: Paris's wrought-iron lattice tower, built by Gustave Eiffel's company for the 1889 World's Fair.
wit: The world's most famous iron hat-rack.
trivia: It was originally meant to stand for only 20 years.
artBrief: Eiffel Tower front view, tapering iron lattice; bronze-brown, pale blue sky, green lawn.

name: Notre-Dame de Paris
summary: A Gothic cathedral on Paris's Île de la Cité, famed for its rose window and gargoyles.
trivia: It reopened in December 2024 after the 2019 fire.
artBrief: Twin square towers facade with central rose window; limestone beige, blue rose window, grey.

name: Palace of Versailles
summary: The opulent royal palace near Paris of Louis XIV, famed for its Hall of Mirrors.
trivia: The Hall of Mirrors contains 357 mirrors.
artBrief: Long golden-gated palace facade with formal garden; cream, gold, green.

name: Mont-Saint-Michel
summary: A tidal island in Normandy crowned by a medieval abbey.
wit: An island when it feels like it.
trivia: At high tide the sea can cut it off from the mainland.
artBrief: Rocky island cone topped by spired abbey surrounded by tidal water; grey stone, blue, sand.

name: Colosseum
summary: Rome's giant ancient amphitheatre, completed in AD 80 for games and spectacles.
trivia: It could hold an estimated 50,000 spectators.
artBrief: Oval ruined amphitheatre with arched tiers, one side broken; travertine beige, blue sky, brown.

name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
summary: The bell tower of Pisa Cathedral, leaning since construction began in 1173.
trivia: It began leaning during construction because of soft ground.
artBrief: Clearly tilted white cylindrical tower with arcades; white marble, green lawn, blue.

name: Sagrada Família
summary: Antoni Gaudí's towering basilica in Barcelona, under construction since 1882.
wit: The world's most patient building site.
trivia: Gaudí worked on it for over 40 years, until his death in 1926.
artBrief: Cluster of tall organic spires with a crane beside; sandstone ochre, green tips, blue sky.

name: Alhambra
summary: A palace and fortress complex in Granada, a masterpiece of Nasrid Moorish architecture.
trivia: Its name comes from Arabic for "the red one".
artBrief: Reddish fortress walls on a hill with snowy mountains behind; red-ochre, green, white.

name: Parthenon
summary: A marble temple to Athena on the Acropolis of Athens, completed in 438 BC.
trivia: Its columns bulge slightly so they look perfectly straight from afar.
artBrief: Columned temple on a rocky hill, partly ruined pediment; marble white, honey, blue sky.

name: Big Ben
summary: The nickname of the Great Bell in the clock tower of London's Palace of Westminster.
trivia: The clock tower was renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012.
artBrief: Gothic clock tower with big white clock face; gold-beige, white, navy sky.

name: Stonehenge
summary: A prehistoric ring of standing stones on Salisbury Plain, built around 3000–2000 BC.
trivia: Its stones align with the sunrise on the summer solstice.
artBrief: Ring of grey standing stones with lintels on green grass at sunrise; grey, green, orange.

name: Hadrian's Wall
summary: A Roman stone wall across northern England, begun in AD 122.
trivia: It ran about 117 km from coast to coast.
artBrief: Low stone wall snaking over green hills; grey, green, cloudy white.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle
summary: A fairy-tale 19th-century castle in Bavaria, built for King Ludwig II.
trivia: It inspired Sleeping Beauty Castle at Disneyland.
artBrief: White castle with slim blue-roofed turrets on a forested cliff; white, slate blue, green.

name: Brandenburg Gate
summary: Berlin's neoclassical gate, completed in 1791, a symbol of German reunification.
trivia: It is topped by the Quadriga, a chariot drawn by four horses.
artBrief: Front view of six-column gate with chariot statue on top; sandstone, green copper, blue.

name: St. Basil's Cathedral
summary: A 16th-century cathedral on Moscow's Red Square, famous for colourful onion domes.
trivia: It was built in the 1550s on the orders of Ivan the Terrible.
artBrief: Cluster of striped onion domes in red, green, blue, gold over red brick.

name: Great Wall of China
summary: A series of fortifications stretching across northern China, built over many centuries.
trivia: Including all its branches, it measures about 21,000 km.
artBrief: Wall with watchtowers snaking over green mountain ridges; grey stone, green, misty blue.

name: Forbidden City
summary: The vast imperial palace in Beijing, home to emperors for nearly 500 years.
trivia: It has nearly 1,000 buildings.
artBrief: Red-walled hall with sweeping yellow-tiled roof; red, golden yellow, white steps.

name: Temple of Heaven
summary: A 15th-century complex in Beijing where emperors prayed for good harvests.
wit: Where harvests were asked for politely.
trivia: Its round Hall of Prayer is built of wood with no nails.
artBrief: Round three-tiered blue-roofed hall on white marble terraces; blue, red, white.

name: Taj Mahal
summary: A white marble mausoleum in Agra built by Emperor Shah Jahan for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
trivia: About 20,000 workers built it over roughly 20 years.
artBrief: White domed mausoleum with four minarets reflected in a pool; white, sky blue, green.

name: Golden Temple
summary: Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar, the holiest gurdwara of Sikhism, covered in gold.
trivia: Its community kitchen serves free meals to tens of thousands of people daily.
artBrief: Golden domed temple on a pool with a causeway; gold, white marble, blue water.

name: Kinkaku-ji
summary: Kyoto's Golden Pavilion, a Zen Buddhist temple covered in gold leaf beside a pond.
wit: Shiny, but very calm about it.
trivia: The current building is a 1955 reconstruction after a fire in 1950.
artBrief: Three-storey gold pavilion reflected in a pond with pine trees; gold, green, blue.

name: Himeji Castle
summary: Japan's finest surviving feudal castle, nicknamed the "White Heron Castle".
wit: A castle dressed for a wedding.
trivia: It survived WWII bombing and many earthquakes largely intact.
artBrief: White multi-tiered castle with grey curved roofs on stone base; white, grey, green.

name: Tokyo Skytree
summary: A broadcasting and observation tower in Tokyo, 634 m tall, opened in 2012.
trivia: It is the tallest tower in the world.
artBrief: Slim white lattice tower with two observation rings against blue sky; white, pale blue, silver.

name: Angkor Wat
summary: A vast 12th-century temple complex in Cambodia, first Hindu and later Buddhist.
trivia: It is the largest religious monument in the world.
artBrief: Five lotus-bud towers reflected in a moat at sunrise; grey stone, orange sky, green.

name: Grand Palace
summary: Bangkok's dazzling royal palace complex, home to the Temple of the Emerald Buddha.
trivia: It was built in 1782 when Bangkok became the capital.
artBrief: Tiered orange-green roofs with golden spires; gold, orange, green.

name: Borobudur
summary: A 9th-century Buddhist temple in Java, built as a giant stepped stone mandala.
wit: A temple you walk up like a spiral.
trivia: It is the largest Buddhist temple in the world.
artBrief: Stepped grey-stone pyramid of terraces with bell-shaped stupas; grey, green jungle, misty blue.

name: Gyeongbokgung
summary: Seoul's main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty, first built in 1395.
trivia: Its name means "Palace Greatly Blessed by Heaven".
artBrief: Painted wooden hall with upturned roof and mountain behind; red, green, blue patterns.

name: Petra
summary: An ancient city carved into rose-red sandstone cliffs by the Nabataeans.
trivia: It was named one of the New Seven Wonders of the World in 2007.
artBrief: Columned facade carved into pink cliff seen through a narrow gorge; rose pink, sand, shadow brown.

name: Burj Khalifa
summary: The world's tallest building, an 828 m skyscraper in Dubai, opened in 2010.
wit: Needs a very long ladder for window cleaning.
trivia: Its tip can be seen from about 95 km away.
artBrief: Very tall stepped silver needle tower with tiny skyline below; silver, blue, sand.

name: Statue of Liberty
summary: A copper statue on Liberty Island in New York Harbor, a gift from France in 1886.
trivia: Its copper skin turned green through natural weathering.
artBrief: Green statue raising a torch, crown spikes, on a pedestal; verdigris green, gold flame, blue.

name: Empire State Building
summary: A 102-storey Art Deco skyscraper in New York City, completed in 1931.
trivia: It was built in just over a year, about 410 days.
artBrief: Art Deco stepped skyscraper with spire at dusk; grey, gold lights, purple sky.

name: CN Tower
summary: Toronto's 553 m communications and observation tower, completed in 1976.
trivia: It was the world's tallest free-standing structure for over 30 years.
artBrief: Concrete needle tower with a pod near the top beside a lake; grey, red light, blue.

name: Teotihuacan
summary: An ancient Mesoamerican city near Mexico City, with the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon.
wit: A city for giants and gods.
trivia: Its main road is called the Avenue of the Dead.
artBrief: Wide stepped Pyramid of the Sun with avenue in front; terracotta, grey, blue sky.

name: Chichén Itzá
summary: A great Maya city in Yucatán, crowned by the stepped pyramid El Castillo.
wit: A pyramid with its own shadow show.
trivia: At the equinoxes, shadows form a serpent sliding down its steps.
artBrief: Four-sided stepped pyramid with central staircase and temple top; grey stone, green, blue.

name: Panama Canal
summary: An 82 km canal across Panama linking the Atlantic and Pacific, opened in 1914.
trivia: Locks lift ships about 26 m to Gatun Lake and back down.
artBrief: Canal lock with ship between gates, green banks; blue, green, orange ship.

name: Christ the Redeemer
summary: The 30 m statue with outstretched arms atop Corcovado mountain in Rio de Janeiro.
trivia: It was completed in 1931 and is often struck by lightning.
artBrief: White statue with outstretched arms on a green peak above the bay; white, green, blue.

name: Machu Picchu
summary: A 15th-century Inca citadel high on an Andean ridge above the Urubamba Valley.
wit: A city with a mountain-top view.
trivia: Its name means "old mountain" in Quechua.
artBrief: Stone terraces and ruins on a ridge with pointed green peak behind; stone grey, green, misty white.

name: Moai
summary: Monolithic human figures carved by the Rapa Nui people on Easter Island.
trivia: There are nearly 1,000 moai on the island.
artBrief: Three stone head-and-torso figures on grass by the sea; dark grey, green, blue.

name: Sydney Opera House
summary: A performing arts centre on Sydney Harbour with sail-shaped roofs, opened in 1973.
wit: Sails that never leave the harbour.
trivia: It was designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon.
artBrief: White overlapping shell roofs on harbour water; white, blue, beige base.

name: Great Zimbabwe
summary: The ruins of a medieval stone city in Zimbabwe, built without mortar.
trivia: Its Great Enclosure walls stand up to 11 m high.
artBrief: Curved dry-stone wall and conical tower in grassland; grey-brown stone, gold grass, blue.

name: Himalayas
summary: Asia's highest mountain range, home to Everest and most of the world's tallest peaks.
trivia: The Himalayas are still rising by a few millimetres each year.
artBrief: Long range of jagged snowy peaks under deep blue sky; white, blue, grey.

name: Mount Everest
summary: Earth's highest mountain above sea level, 8,849 m, on the border of Nepal and China.
trivia: Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary first reached the summit in 1953.
artBrief: Single pyramid snowy peak with summit plume, prayer flags in front; white, blue, multicolour flags.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
summary: Africa's highest mountain, a dormant volcano in Tanzania rising to 5,895 m.
trivia: It is the world's tallest free-standing mountain.
artBrief: Broad flat-topped snowy volcano above savanna with acacia; white, blue, gold.

name: Andes
summary: The longest continental mountain range, running along South America's west coast.
trivia: Aconcagua, at 6,961 m, is the highest peak in the Andes.
artBrief: Long chain of brown and snow peaks with a llama silhouette; brown, white, blue.

name: Alps
summary: Europe's great mountain range, stretching across eight countries from France to Slovenia.
trivia: Mont Blanc, about 4,806 m, is the highest peak of the Alps.
artBrief: Snowy peaks over green meadow with a wooden chalet; white, green, blue.

name: Matterhorn
summary: A pyramid-shaped Alpine peak of 4,478 m on the Swiss–Italian border.
wit: The mountain that looks like a mountain.
trivia: It was first climbed in 1865 by Edward Whymper's party.
artBrief: Single sharp hooked pyramid peak, snowy, with pink alpenglow; white, pink, grey.

name: Mount Fuji
summary: Japan's highest mountain, a 3,776 m volcano with a famously symmetrical cone.
trivia: It last erupted in 1707.
artBrief: Symmetrical snow-capped cone with cherry blossom branch; blue-grey, white, pink.

name: Mount Vesuvius
summary: An active volcano overlooking the Bay of Naples, famous for burying Pompeii.
trivia: Its eruption in AD 79 buried Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash.
artBrief: Wide two-humped volcano with smoke plume above a blue bay; grey-brown, blue, white smoke.

name: Uluru
summary: A giant sandstone monolith in central Australia, sacred to the Aṉangu people.
trivia: Climbing Uluru has been banned since 2019 out of respect.
artBrief: Long rounded red rock on flat desert at sunset; red-orange, purple sky, ochre.

name: Grand Canyon
summary: A vast Arizona canyon carved by the Colorado River, up to about 1.8 km deep.
wit: A very deep scratch in the Earth.
trivia: Its rock layers record nearly 2 billion years of Earth's history.
artBrief: Layered red-orange canyon walls with a thin river below; red, orange, blue.

name: Victoria Falls
summary: A huge waterfall on the Zambezi River between Zambia and Zimbabwe.
trivia: Locally it is called Mosi-oa-Tunya, "the smoke that thunders".
artBrief: Wide curtain waterfall with rising mist and rainbow; white, blue, green.

name: Angel Falls
summary: The world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, dropping 979 m in Venezuela.
wit: The longest drop in the world.
trivia: It is named after US aviator Jimmie Angel, who flew over it in 1933.
artBrief: Thin white ribbon of water falling from a flat-topped cliff; white, dark green, grey.

name: Niagara Falls
summary: A group of three waterfalls on the Niagara River between Canada and the USA.
trivia: In 1901 Annie Edson Taylor became the first to go over it in a barrel.
artBrief: Horseshoe-shaped falls with a small boat in the mist; blue, white, green.

name: Great Barrier Reef
summary: The world's largest coral reef system, stretching over 2,300 km off Queensland.
wit: A city of coral, visible from space.
trivia: It is the largest structure built by living things and can be seen from space.
artBrief: Turquoise water with colourful coral and a clownfish, top view; turquoise, coral pink, orange.

name: Sahara
summary: The largest hot desert on Earth, covering much of North Africa.
wit: Sand, with more sand on the side.
trivia: Its name comes from the Arabic word for "desert".
artBrief: Rolling golden dunes with a camel silhouette under the sun; gold, orange, pale blue.

name: Lake Baikal
summary: A Siberian rift lake, the world's deepest and oldest freshwater lake.
trivia: It holds about 20% of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water.
artBrief: Clear turquoise ice cracks on a lake with distant hills; turquoise, white, dark green.

name: Amazon Rainforest
summary: The largest tropical rainforest on Earth, spread over nine countries, mostly Brazil.
trivia: About 10% of all known species live in the Amazon.
artBrief: Dense green canopy with a winding brown river and a red macaw; green, brown, red.

name: Galápagos Islands
summary: Volcanic Pacific islands of Ecuador, famous for giant tortoises and Darwin's studies.
trivia: Charles Darwin visited in 1835 aboard HMS Beagle.
artBrief: Giant tortoise on black volcanic rock with blue sea; brown, black, blue.

name: Nile
summary: A great river flowing north through eastern Africa into the Mediterranean, the lifeline of Egypt.
wit: Flows north and doesn't care what you think.
trivia: At about 6,650 km it is often listed as the world's longest river.
artBrief: Blue river winding north through yellow desert with green banks and a felucca sail; blue, gold, green.

name: Amazon River
summary: The giant river of South America's rainforest, with the greatest flow of any river.
wit: So big it has its own weather.
trivia: It carries about a fifth of all river water flowing into the oceans.
artBrief: Wide brown river through dense green jungle, top view; brown, green, blue sky.

name: Mississippi River
summary: A major US river flowing about 3,770 km from Minnesota south past New Orleans to the sea.
trivia: Its basin drains all or part of 31 US states.
artBrief: Broad river bend with a white paddle steamer; brown-blue, white, red paddle.

name: Yangtze River
summary: Asia's longest river, flowing about 6,300 km across China to the East China Sea.
trivia: The Three Gorges Dam on the Yangtze is the world's largest power station.
artBrief: River between steep misty gorge cliffs with a junk boat; blue-green, grey, mist white.

name: Ganges
summary: A great river of northern India and Bangladesh, held sacred in Hinduism.
wit: A river of prayers and lamps.
trivia: The Ganges–Brahmaputra delta is the largest delta in the world.
artBrief: River at dusk with small floating oil lamps on the water; deep blue, orange glow, gold.

name: Danube
summary: Europe's second-longest river, flowing from Germany's Black Forest to the Black Sea.
trivia: It flows through or along 10 countries, more than any other river.
artBrief: Blue river curving through green hills under a stone bridge; blue, green, grey.

name: Rhine
summary: A major European river that rises in the Swiss Alps and flows to the North Sea.
wit: Castles on both banks, barges in the middle.
trivia: The Rhine passes through Lake Constance on its way north.
artBrief: River with a hilltop castle and vineyard terraces; blue, green, sandstone.

name: Thames
summary: The river flowing through London, the longest river entirely in England.
trivia: Frost fairs were held on the frozen Thames until 1814.
artBrief: River curving past a bascule bridge silhouette; grey-blue, stone, navy.

name: Seine
summary: The river through Paris, flowing past Notre-Dame and the Eiffel Tower to the English Channel.
trivia: Thirty-seven bridges cross the Seine in Paris.
artBrief: River with an arched stone bridge and bookstall stand; blue, cream, green.

name: Tiber
summary: The river of Rome, flowing from the Apennines to the Tyrrhenian Sea.
trivia: Legend says Romulus and Remus were set adrift on the Tiber.
artBrief: Green-brown river with Roman arched bridge and pine tree; olive, terracotta, blue.

name: Volga
summary: Europe's longest river, flowing about 3,530 km through Russia to the Caspian Sea.
wit: Europe's longest, by a long way.
trivia: Russians often call it "Mother Volga".
artBrief: Very wide calm river with birch trees on the bank; blue, white bark, green.

name: Mekong
summary: A great Southeast Asian river flowing from the Tibetan Plateau to Vietnam's delta.
trivia: The Mekong flows through six countries.
artBrief: River with a floating market canoe full of fruit; brown water, green, orange fruit.

name: Zambezi
summary: Southern Africa's longest east-flowing river, home of Victoria Falls.
trivia: Victoria Falls and Lake Kariba both lie on the Zambezi.
artBrief: River rushing to a cliff edge with mist rising; blue, white, green.

name: Murray River
summary: Australia's longest river, flowing about 2,500 km through the south-east.
trivia: Paddle steamers still cruise the Murray today.
artBrief: Ochre-banked river with gum trees and a small paddle steamer; brown, eucalyptus green, red.

name: St. Lawrence River
summary: A great river linking the Great Lakes to the Atlantic, past Montreal and Quebec City.
trivia: The St. Lawrence Seaway lets ships sail from the Atlantic to the Great Lakes.
artBrief: Wide river with a cargo ship and red maple trees on shore; blue, red, green.

name: Rio Grande
summary: A North American river that forms much of the border between Mexico and the USA.
trivia: In Mexico it is called the Río Bravo.
artBrief: Shallow river winding through desert scrub; blue, tan, sage green.

name: Colorado River
summary: A south-western US river that carved the Grand Canyon over millions of years.
trivia: The Hoover Dam holds back the Colorado to form Lake Mead.
artBrief: Green river at the bottom of red canyon walls; green, red, orange.

name: Río de la Plata
summary: The broad estuary of the Paraná and Uruguay rivers between Argentina and Uruguay.
wit: A river so wide it looks like sea.
trivia: It is up to about 220 km wide, among the widest estuaries on Earth.
artBrief: Very wide brown estuary meeting blue sea with a distant city line; brown, blue, silver.

name: Orinoco
summary: One of South America's longest rivers, flowing through Venezuela to the Atlantic.
trivia: It is home to the critically endangered Orinoco crocodile.
artBrief: Jungle river with a crocodile snout on the surface; olive, brown, green.

name: Tagus
summary: The longest river of the Iberian Peninsula, flowing through Spain and Portugal to Lisbon.
wit: Iberia's longest road to the sea.
trivia: Lisbon's Vasco da Gama Bridge over the Tagus is over 12 km long.
artBrief: River mouth with long low bridge and yellow tram on the bank; blue, yellow, white.

name: Sushi
summary: A Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, seafood or vegetables.
trivia: Washoku, traditional Japanese cuisine, joined UNESCO's heritage list in 2013.
artBrief: Two nigiri pieces and a maki roll on a wooden board; white rice, salmon orange, nori black.

name: Paella
summary: A Valencian rice dish cooked in a wide, shallow pan with saffron.
trivia: The crispy rice at the bottom of the pan is called socarrat.
artBrief: Wide two-handled pan of yellow rice with prawns and lemon; yellow, red, green.

name: Tacos
summary: Folded corn tortillas filled with meat, beans, salsa and more, a Mexican staple.
trivia: Corn tortillas have been eaten in Mexico for thousands of years.
artBrief: Three folded tacos with salsa and lime wedge; corn yellow, red, green.

name: Curry
summary: A family of spiced South Asian dishes with rich sauces built on spice blends.
trivia: The word may come from Tamil "kari", meaning sauce.
artBrief: Bowl of orange curry beside rice and naan; orange, white, brown.

name: Kimchi
summary: Korea's spicy fermented vegetable dish, usually made with napa cabbage and chili.
trivia: Kimjang, the communal making of kimchi, is on UNESCO's heritage list.
artBrief: Red-orange fermented cabbage in a clay jar; red, pale green, brown.

name: Pho
summary: Vietnam's fragrant noodle soup with clear broth, rice noodles and fresh herbs.
trivia: Pho is traditionally eaten for breakfast in Vietnam.
artBrief: Steaming bowl of noodle soup with herbs and chopsticks; amber broth, green herbs, white.

name: Pad Thai
summary: Thailand's stir-fried rice noodle dish with egg, tamarind, peanuts and lime.
trivia: Pad Thai was promoted as a national dish in Thailand in the 1930s–40s.
artBrief: Plate of stir-fried noodles with lime wedge and peanuts; tan, green, orange.

name: Feijoada
summary: Brazil's hearty black bean and pork stew, served with rice and orange slices.
trivia: In Brazil it is traditionally eaten on Wednesdays and Saturdays.
artBrief: Clay pot of dark bean stew with orange slices and rice; black-brown, orange, white.

name: Ceviche
summary: Peru's dish of raw fish cured in lime juice with chili and red onion.
trivia: Peru celebrates National Ceviche Day on 28 June.
artBrief: Bowl of white fish cubes with red onion, chili and corn; white, purple-red, yellow.

name: Poutine
summary: A Quebec dish of fries topped with cheese curds and hot gravy.
trivia: Poutine was created in rural Quebec in the 1950s.
artBrief: Box of fries with white curds and brown gravy; gold, white, brown.

name: Fish and Chips
summary: Battered fried fish with thick-cut chips, a British seaside classic.
wit: Best eaten with a seagull nearby.
trivia: It was one of the few foods not rationed in Britain during WWII.
artBrief: Battered fish and chips on paper with a lemon wedge; golden, white paper, yellow.

name: Couscous
summary: Steamed semolina granules served with stew, a staple of North Africa and Morocco.
trivia: Couscous traditions joined UNESCO's list in 2020, shared by four countries.
artBrief: Cone-shaped clay tagine lid beside a mound of couscous with vegetables; terracotta, yellow, orange.

name: Injera
summary: Ethiopia's spongy sourdough flatbread made from teff, used to scoop up stews.
wit: Plate, spoon and bread in one.
trivia: Teff, the grain used for injera, has some of the tiniest seeds of any cereal.
artBrief: Large round spongy flatbread with colourful stew dollops, top view; beige, red, green.

name: Fondue
summary: A Swiss pot of melted cheese and wine, shared by dipping bread on long forks.
trivia: The Swiss Cheese Union promoted fondue as a national dish in the 1930s.
artBrief: Red pot of melted yellow cheese with bread on a long fork; red, yellow, brown.

name: Moussaka
summary: A Greek baked dish of layered aubergine, spiced meat and creamy béchamel.
trivia: The modern Greek version was popularised by chef Nikolaos Tselementes in the 1920s.
artBrief: Square slice showing purple aubergine and meat layers under golden top; purple, brown, gold.

name: Peking Duck
summary: A Beijing dish of roast duck with crisp skin, served with thin pancakes and sauce.
trivia: Peking duck has been prepared in Beijing since imperial times.
artBrief: Glossy roast duck slices with pancakes and spring onions; mahogany, cream, green.

name: Rio Carnival
summary: Rio de Janeiro's huge pre-Lent festival of samba parades, feathers and floats.
trivia: Samba schools parade in the Sambadrome, opened in 1984.
artBrief: Feathered carnival headdress with sequins; gold, magenta, green, blue.

name: Day of the Dead
summary: Mexico's festival honouring departed loved ones with altars, marigolds and sugar skulls.
trivia: It is celebrated on 1 and 2 November.
artBrief: Decorated sugar skull with marigold flowers; white, orange, pink, turquoise.

name: Oktoberfest
summary: Munich's giant folk festival, held most years since 1810.
trivia: It began as a celebration of a royal wedding in 1810.
artBrief: Pretzel and a beer stein on a blue-white diamond tablecloth; gold, blue, white.

name: Diwali
summary: The festival of lights celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs and Jains with lamps, sweets and fireworks.
trivia: Homes are lit with small clay oil lamps called diyas.
artBrief: Glowing clay oil lamps on a colourful rangoli pattern; orange flame, magenta, gold.

name: Chinese New Year
summary: The Spring Festival marking the lunar new year, with red lanterns, dumplings and dragon dances.
trivia: Each year is linked to one of 12 zodiac animals.
artBrief: Two red paper lanterns with gold tassels and firecracker string; red, gold.

name: Songkran
summary: Thailand's New Year festival in April, famous for joyful water fights.
wit: A new year that soaks you.
trivia: Songkran is celebrated from 13 to 15 April.
artBrief: Water splash from a bowl with jasmine flowers; blue, white, gold.

name: La Tomatina
summary: A festival in Buñol, Spain, where crowds throw tomatoes at each other.
trivia: It is held on the last Wednesday of August.
artBrief: Tomato bursting with red splatter; red, green stem, white.

name: Hanami
summary: The Japanese custom of picnicking under blooming cherry blossoms in spring.
trivia: Forecasters track the "cherry blossom front" as it moves north each spring.
artBrief: Cherry blossom branch over a picnic mat; pink, brown, light blue.

name: Inti Raymi
summary: The Inca Festival of the Sun, revived each June in Cusco, Peru.
trivia: It is held on 24 June, near the southern winter solstice.
artBrief: Golden sun disc with rays over Andean stone wall; gold, red, grey.

name: Carnival of Venice
summary: Venice's pre-Lent festival famous for elaborate masks and costumes.
trivia: Masks once let Venetians of all classes mingle anonymously.
artBrief: Ornate gold and white Venetian eye mask with feather; gold, white, deep purple.

name: Kimono
summary: Japan's traditional T-shaped robe with wide sleeves, tied with an obi sash.
trivia: "Kimono" literally means "thing to wear".
artBrief: Folded T-shaped robe with floral pattern and wide sash; indigo, pink, gold obi.

name: Sari
summary: A long, unstitched drape of fabric worn elegantly across India and South Asia.
trivia: A sari is usually 4.5 to 9 metres long.
artBrief: Flowing draped fabric with gold border, shown on a stand; magenta, gold, emerald.

name: Hanbok
summary: Korea's traditional dress with a short jacket and a full, high-waisted skirt.
trivia: Koreans often wear hanbok for Chuseok and Lunar New Year.
artBrief: Short jacket with long ribbon tie above bell-shaped skirt; pink jacket, blue skirt, white ribbon.

name: Flamenco
summary: Andalusia's passionate art of song, guitar, dance and rhythmic hand-clapping.
trivia: Flamenco was added to UNESCO's heritage list in 2010.
artBrief: Red ruffled dress mid-twirl with a fan; red, black, white polka dots.

name: Tango
summary: A dramatic partner dance and music born in Buenos Aires and Montevideo.
trivia: Tango was added to UNESCO's heritage list in 2009.
artBrief: Silhouette of two dancers in a dip with a rose; black, red, warm amber.
